decision: Adopt a fail-closed evidence gate for the first real-Qubes phase: intended read-only service must be allowed, wrong service/identity/auth/framing must be denied, the allowed response must verify Ed25519 attestation and byte/framing bounds, and MissionStore/DurableRequestJournal must remain unchanged.
winner: offline qualification report built from real qrexec observations

comparisons.approach: promote the existing Node probe tests directly to readiness evidence
comparisons.correctness: weak: proves application behavior but not Qubes policy routing

comparisons.approach: add a state-changing qrexec smoke immediately
comparisons.correctness: can test more of the stack but conflates policy and MissionQueue failures
comparisons.robustness: worse blast radius because first VM-crossing test mutates state

comparisons.approach: offline qualification report built from real qrexec observations
comparisons.correctness: strong: explicitly gates routing, deployment identity, attestation, framing and zero mutation
comparisons.robustness: fail-closed and preserves separation between transport acceptance and MissionQueue mutation
comparisons.latencyResourceUse: no production round trips, daemon, database or worker changes
comparisons.regressionRisk: low and isolated to Slice 2 qualification
comparisons.qa: deterministic contract tests plus later real-Qubes evidence ingestion

lessons: A read-only application probe alone cannot prove Qubes policy routing.
The first real-Qubes gate should detect wrong-service authorization before any MissionQueue mutation is possible.
Evidence integrity digests make reports tamper-evident but do not replace Ed25519 protocol authenticity.
Zero mutation must be supported by before/after durable-state evidence, not assumed from operation naming.
safety: Synthetic/defensive qualification only. No financial transactions, payment data, fraud flows, or weakened security controls.
